ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a substituted benzene ring, with two adjacent R¹O/alkoxy substituents on the benzene ring, and with a -CH2-CH2-NH2 side chain connected to the other side of the benzene ring. On the right side is a protonated carbonyl-like fragment, where the carbon is connected to H and R², and the carbon forms a double bond with an oxygen that bears a positive charge and is connected to H; a reaction arrow is also drawn in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrow. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrow, the protonated carbonyl fragment on the right is represented with wildcard R² as *C=[OH+]. The left aromatic fragment needs to encode the two R¹ positions as oxygen substituents connected to wildcards, and preserve the relative substitution relationship of the -CCN side chain on the benzene ring, and can be written as *Oc1ccc(CCN)cc1O*. The two fragments are not bonded in the static structure, so they are connected with a dot, giving *C=[OH+].*Oc1ccc(CCN)cc1O*.

method.method_draft: First transcribe the static connectivity from the image while ignoring the arrows. Encode the right-hand protonated carbonyl fragment as an unspecified substituent attached to a carbonyl carbon bearing H and double-bonded to protonated oxygen: *C=[OH+]. Join the two disconnected components with a dot to obtain *C=[OH+].*Oc1ccc(CCN)cc1O*.
